item: the test job installs original-awk and gawk so the two launcher awk tests run, and prints skip reasons with -rs
summary: tests/test_launcher_records_race.py::test_the_filter_records_under_the_one_true_awk skips unless original-awk is on PATH, and tests/test_launcher_stderr.py::test_the_filter_gives_the_same_record_under_every_awk_it_may_meet skips unless two of mawk, gawk, original-awk and busybox are. The skip-reason audit (2026-10-29) found both skipping with mawk alone, which is what the runner image is inferred to carry. The test job now installs original-awk and gawk in a step after the tesseract step. gawk registers itself as the awk alternative at priority 10 against mawk's 5, so a bare install would move every other launcher test and every shell script from mawk to gawk; the step records readlink -f /usr/bin/awk first, restores it with update-alternatives --set awk, and prints what was installed before and the default before and after. The same job's pytest line gains -rs, so each skip's file, line and reason are in the log (a grouped block before the result line; no outcome changes). Measured on a scratch tree with the two awks on PATH: the two launcher files give 98 passed, 4 skipped (the four are pwsh) against 96 passed, 6 skipped with mawk alone, and the 16 test files that read ci.yml pass with the step in it (496 passed, 32 skipped). Stated limits: not measured on a runner, so whether the image already carried gawk or busybox is read from the step's own first line in the PR run, not from here; the step fails if /usr/bin/awk is not a registered alternative (Ubuntu images register mawk), which is a loud red rather than a silent change; the skip-count delta of the test job is read from the PR run's pytest summary. Evidence: /mnt/project-files/export-lane/awk-step-2026-10-29/MEASURED.md.
